conventional units) 
• Elevated levels: dehydration 
• Decreased levels: chronic disease, malabsorption, 
malnutrition with low protein, or dilution by IV fluids 
• Follow-up diagnostics: prealbumin, blood urea nitrogen, or 
zinc (deficiency increases risk for pneumonia [Keller, 2019]) 
Prealbumin 
• 180–450 mg/L 
(18–45 mg/dL 
conventional units) 
• Elevated levels: chronic kidney disease, steroid use, or 
alcohol use disorder 
• Decreased levels: malnutrition, liver disease, infection, or 
inflammation 
• Follow-up diagnostics: nutritional assessment, hemoglobin, 
and anemia evaluation (iron, transferrin, folate, and vitamin 
B12)
